steps.body: Friendly pairing is a habit, not a trick: before any long sum, spend three seconds scanning for ones that complete each other.
steps.narration: Friendly pairing is a habit, not a trick: before any long sum, spend three seconds scanning for ones that complete each other.

widget.prompt: Tap the friendly pair in 46, 23, 14: the ones that make a ten.

hotspots.feedback: 23 carries 3 ones — 6 needs a 4, and 3 is not it.

widget.missFeedback: Look at the ONES digits — the friendly pair is the one whose ones complete a ten.
widget.successFeedback: That pair's ones complete a ten — banking it first makes the rest easy.

predict.prompt: 46 + 23 + 14: scan the ones. Which two complete a ten?
predict.reveal: 6 + 4 = 10, so 46 + 14 = 60 — the scan found free simplicity.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents g2n friendly pairs.
invariants: Regrouping addends changes the ORDER of joining, never the total — every staging of the sum must land on the same number for g2n friendly pairs.
misconceptions: Believing the grouping or order of addends can change a sum, or letting an addend join twice or not at all while restaging.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: Which single change to the staging would actually change the total — and which only changes the path?

explanationVariants: The scan comes before the adding.

widget.prompt: In 13 + 24 + 27, which two addends make the friendliest pair to add FIRST?

options.label: 13 and 27 — their ones make a ten
options.feedback: Correct — 3 + 7 = 10, so 13 + 27 lands on a clean ten and the rest joins easily.

options.label: 13 and 24 — they come first
options.feedback: Order on the page is not a strategy; their ones (3 + 4) miss the ten.

options.label: 24 and 27 — the biggest two
options.feedback: Size alone does not help; those ones (4 + 7) do not complete a ten.

options.label: 13 and 18 — they look alike
options.feedback: 18 is not even in this sum — a pair must come from the addends you actually have.
